title: Ashtpadi 7, salok: the holy company
hookLine: the salok praises the company of the holy

cards: Some people walk into a room and make it a little easier to be good. Nobody feels judged around them. Conversations get kinder; the complaining slows; the laughter gets more honest.
People leave having been a better version of themselves for an hour, without trying. For several ashtpadis, Sukhmani has talked about the Giver and the gifts.
Now, in the seventh, it turns to people: the holy, and what happens to us in their company.

teach.b: The salok has four short lines. First: the Supreme Lord is agam, out of reach, and agaadh, too deep to sound. Second: whoever speaks of Him is set free.
Third: listen, friend, Nanak prays. And fourth: saadh janaa kee acharaj kathaa.
The story of the holy ones is wondrous.
Saadh, or saadhoo, is a holy person, someone whose life has been shaped by the Name. Acharaj is wonder, the feeling of seeing something you didn't think was possible. Notice the order.
The salok starts with God beyond reach, and ends with people you can actually sit beside.
That's the bridge this ashtpadi builds: the One too deep to sound becomes nearer in the company of those who remember Him.

In Sikh life that has a concrete shape: the sangat, the congregation, singing together in the gurdwara and eating side by side in the langar. Over the next days, the ashtpadi lists what happens in that company.
And this is where the week ends. Six days ago, if He took the ten, and the mind where God tastes sweet. The banker's capital, lent, not owned.
The five thieves and grace that clears the house. Jih prasaad over dinner, the body and the home. Every comfort a gift.
A week of the Giver. Now, the Giver's people.

how: Sikhs gather as sangat, the congregation, in the gurdwara to sing and hear the Guru's word and to eat together in langar; ashtpadi seven of Sukhmani Sahib praises that holy company.

o: a holy person shaped by the Name
a story told to teach a lesson

games.q: the seventh salok — tap the pairs.

s: the salok begins with the holy ones and ends with God
it begins with God beyond reach and ends with the wondrous story of the holy.
the salok says whoever speaks of God is set free
in Sikh life, holy company has a concrete shape: the sangat
the congregation singing and eating side by side.

games.q: the salok has called God out of reach, too deep to sound. where does it point next?
o: to the wondrous story of the holy ones.
games.why: saadh janaa kee acharaj kathaa: the bridge to the One beyond reach runs through the company of the holy.

practice: Bring to mind one person in whose presence you become a little better, a grandparent, a teacher, a friend, someone you sat beside once and never forgot, and remember one thing they said, or the way they listened.
Notice what your body does as you remember them; maybe the shoulders soften, maybe the jaw unclenches. If you pray, give thanks for them, and breathe out whatever you don't need to carry.

wordCard.voice: Acharaj, wonder. The salok calls God beyond reach, and the story of the holy ones wondrous.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: acharaj, wonder, the wondrous; the salok's word for the story of the holy.

carryVoice: Your line: good company. Some people make good a little easier, just by being there. A week, done.

sources.work: Guru Granth Sahib (Guru Arjan, Gauri Sukhmani)
